finding.claim: Unauthenticated SSRF: the /fetch handler passes the `target` query parameter straight to http.Get and returns the response body to the caller. An attacker can reach internal services, loopback, and cloud metadata endpoints (e.g. http://169.254.169.254/) and read the responses. Error text from failed requests is also returned, which leaks connection details.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) at main.go:16, with the body copied to the response at main.go:22

trace.note: /fetch registered with http.HandleFunc and no auth middleware
target read from the query string
http.Get(target) called with the raw value
upstream response body copied back to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, no host allowlist, no private/loopback/link-local IP blocking, no redirect restriction, no timeout, and no authentication. The `allowed` map is used only in safeFetch, not in fetch.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-16 passes the query param `target` unvalidated to http.Get and main.go:22 returns the body (main.go:18 returns err.Error()), and /fetch is registered at main.go:41 with no auth or host check (the `allowed` map is only used in safeFetch at main.go:27).
